result.summary: 1956543 EXPANSION NETWORK (priority 0, 19 working days old against a 7-day target, 12 days overdue) leads the city_priority_list. The 283 unprioritised orders require immediate triage, with SIGNWORKS JOB – CHILD (FABRICATION) the most frequent type (155 orders).

claims.statement: city_priority_list ranks the three most urgent open work orders: 1956543 EXPANSION NETWORK (priority 0, 19 working days old against a 7-day target, 12 days overdue), 1972786 CONSTRUCTION INSPECTION (priority 0, 5 days old, on target), and 1968061 SIGNWORKS JOB – CHILD (FABRICATION) (priority 0, 9 days old, within 36-day target).

Finding f1 covers 281 open orders in the TOA asset group under priority level 0, with 0 past SLA target (target 36 days from history); the top orders for dispatch are SIGNWORKS JOB – CHILD (FABRICATION), SIGNWORKS JOB - PARENT, and SIGNWORKS JOB – CHILD (INSTALLATION), all 9 working days old.

Finding f2 covers 279 open orders in the TOA-S&M category under priority level 0, with 0 past SLA target (target 36 days from history); the top orders for dispatch are SIGNWORKS JOB – CHILD (FABRICATION), SIGNWORKS JOB - PARENT, and SIGNWORKS JOB – CHILD (INSTALLATION), all 9 working days old.
283 open orders have no priority assigned and require triage before dispatch; they constitute 100% of all open orders.
Ages include 1 public holiday (Labour Day) and 3 weather-impacted working days; the overdue count of 1 remains unchanged after net-of-weather adjustment.

For the TOA asset group, the median time to close within cap is 2.0 working days (p75 36) based on 180 closed samples; however, weather effect data are insufficient (enough_data false) to determine if weather slows closures.

priority_list.address: PENNSYLVANIA AVENUE SE AND MINNESOTA AVENUE SE

caveats: SLA targets: 2 of the 2 asset-group and priority cells used in this triage use the 75th percentile of closures within 60 working days from a sample of 289 closed historical orders; the rest are assumptions, and priority weights are assumptions. The sample is small, so treat targets as indicative, not DC policy.
Priority 5 is treated as the most urgent (EMERGENCY orders carry it in this extract); the source does not document the priority scale.
The data covers 3 August to 8 September 2026 only, and ages are measured to the last work order raised.
The ranking says where the weighted backlog and overdue work sit; it cannot see crew capacity, contracts or budgets, which are not in the data.
283 open orders (100%) have no priority; they are scored as medium urgency until someone triages them.

evidence.sql: SELECT MAX(initiated_date) AS as_of, MIN(initiated_date) AS first_day, COUNT(1) AS n FROM fixfirst.work_orders WHERE record_set = 'active_fy2026'

SELECT COALESCE(w.asset_group, '(none)') AS member, COUNT(1) AS n_orders, SUM(COALESCE(p.weight, 1)) AS points FROM fixfirst.work_orders w LEFT JOIN fixfirst.sla_policy p ON p.asset_group = w.asset_group AND p.priority_level = COALESCE(w.priority, 0) WHERE w.status IN ('OPEN', '01-ASSIGNED', '02-INPROGRESS', 'PENDING') GROUP BY COALESCE(w.asset_group, '(none)')
